cards.text: Hezekiah, king of Judah, has just been through a serious illness. Then a delivery arrives from a king with a name that takes a while: Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon. I tried saying it three times fast, friend, and my mustache tied itself in a knot.

cards.question: The king of Babylon sends Hezekiah letters and a ___.
Why does the king of Babylon send letters and a gift to Hezekiah?

answers.text: He heard Hezekiah had been ill
Hezekiah had sent him gifts first

cards.text: Hezekiah welcomes the envoys the king of Babylon sent. And then, friend, he gives them the TOUR.

cards.question: Hezekiah gives the envoys from Babylon a tour. How much does he show them?

answers.text: Everything in his palace and kingdom
Only his treasure house and its gold
Only the gifts for their king

cards.question: Hezekiah shows the envoys from Babylon his armory.

cards.text: The silver, the gold, the spices, the precious oil, the armory, the storehouses. Friend, that's a stranger dropping off a get-well card, and you pull out your phone and scroll them through your WHOLE bank account.
Then Isaiah the prophet comes to the king and asks, "Where did those men come from, and what did they say to you?" That's the kind of question that makes my mustache SWEAT.

cards.question: Hezekiah tells Isaiah the men came from Babylon. When Isaiah asks what they've seen, Hezekiah says there is nothing among his treasures he didn't show them.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD:" I bet the whole room went quiet.

cards.question: The LORD says the time will surely come when everything in Hezekiah's palace will be carried off to ___.
The LORD says a few of the treasures will be left behind in Hezekiah's palace.
Isaiah says it goes beyond treasure. Some of Hezekiah's ___ will be taken away to the palace of the king of ___.
Isaiah has just told Hezekiah that some of his own flesh and blood will be taken to be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon. What does Hezekiah say back?

answers.text: The word of the LORD is good
Ask the LORD to spare my family
This word is too heavy to bear

cards.question: Hezekiah calls the word of the LORD good. What is he thinking?

answers.text: There will be peace in his lifetime
The LORD will change His mind
His sons will win the treasure back

cards.text: He thinks, "Will there not at least be peace and security in my lifetime?" Friend, that's the snooze button. The alarm doesn't go away. It just goes off LATER.
The rest of what Hezekiah did, and all his might, is written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. But the writer still gives a shout-out to two big projects.

cards.question: Hezekiah built a pool and a tunnel to bring water into the city.

cards.text: And Hezekiah rested with his fathers. Now one of his sons takes the throne.

cards.question: Hezekiah has rested with his fathers. Which of his sons reigns in his place?

findings.problem: The opening card says Hezekiah 'has just been through a serious illness' and then says a delivery arrives. That is the reason for the gift, so card 3 (why the king of Babylon sends letters and a gift) is answered before it is asked.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'Serious illness' comes from the previous passage. 2 Kings 20:1 says he was 'mortally ill', while 20:12 says only 'illness'. The card cites only 2 Kings 20:12, so this outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke is about how hard a foreign king's name is to say ('I tried saying it three times fast... my mustache tied itself in a knot'). It is self-deprecating, but its target is the length and sound of a non-Hebrew name.
findings.question: Are jokes about a Bible person's name being long or hard to pronounce allowed? Or do they fall under the ban on jokes about nationality or accents, or under the rule that humor about Bible people should look at their human situation with respect?

findings.problem: This story card comes after cards 5 and 6 have already asked about verse 13, and it goes back over the same tour. It does not move the passage forward. The list of silver, gold, spices and oil could ride on card 4 instead.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This is the second mustache joke out of the walkthrough's few jokes (card 1's knotted mustache, card 8's sweating mustache). That makes the mustache the main source of the humor.

rule.text: The mustache is a fact about him, not his main source of jokes.

findings.problem: Card 15 has already asked and answered what Hezekiah thinks in verse 19. This card only restates that thought and adds a joke. It is a recap card and does not move the passage forward.

In verse 20, the pool and the tunnel are part of what 'is written in the Book of the Chronicles'. The card says the rest is written there 'But the writer still gives a shout-out to two big projects', which sets the projects against that book. This changes how the text connects the two things.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Now one of his sons takes the throne' (and card 20's 'Which of his sons') implies Hezekiah had several sons. Verse 21 says only 'his son Manasseh reigned in his place.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
